Corner of the mouth to the earlobe (or center of mouth to angle of jaw)
How do we measure for proper insertion of an NPA?
Tip of the nose to the earlobe; select the largest diameter that fits the nostril

After placing pads in anterolateral placement, you see a jewelry piercing on the patient at the navel. What should you do next?
Nothing — piercings at the navel do not interfere with anterolateral pad placement; continue without moving pads or removing jewelry
What should be done immediately following a shock?
Resume CPR immediately (begin with chest compressions)
You feel a faint pulse after checking for 5-10 sec. Your next action is to
continue CPR — a pulse must be clearly felt to stop compressions; an uncertain pulse should be treated as absent

The primary focus of a CPR Coach is ensuring what?
High-quality CPR — correct rate (100–120/min), adequate depth (≥2 inches), full chest recoil, minimal interruptions, and no excessive ventilation
What does CCF mean?   Chest  Compression  Fraction.
CCF should be 60 %.   Ideally CCF should be 80 %
Minimize interruptions to compressions — limit pulse checks, pre-charge the defibrillator during CPR, and resume compressions immediately after a shock

What are the Signs and Symptoms of a Stroke? (CPHSS)
F  Facial droop — ask patient to smile; assess for asymmetry
A  Arm drift — ask patient to hold both arms out; watch for one drifting down
S  Speech — slurred, garbled, or inability to speak/understand
T  Time — note time of last known well; activate stroke protocol immediately
Diagnostically, is important to run these tests:
1.  12-Lead ECG  to rule out Myocardial Infarction
2.  Blood glucose  to rule out Hypoglycemia.
Upon arrival to the ED, a Non-Contrast CT of the brain should be completed
w/in 20 minutes & interpreted by radiology within 45 min of arrival to ED.
